newsitem.title: USA: Oregon Treasurer backs initiative reform - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Oregon Treasurer backs initiative reform - spokesman.

text.p: Oregon state Treasurer Jim Hill will back a proposal to reform to the state's initiative process, a spokesman said on Tuesday, adding that the changes could boost Oregon's credit rating.

Hill spokesman Michael Parker said the treasurer would support a proposal by Oregon House Speaker Lynn Lundquist to create a 12-member committee to review initiatives, hold hearings and issue a financial impact report on the measures.
Parker said Hill and Lundquist plan to meet with Moody's Investors Service Inc officials later on Tuesday to discuss the proposal and the state's bond rating.

The so-called Citizen Initiative Review Committee would consist of 12 members -- four appointed by the governor, four appointed by the president of the Senate and four appointed by the speaker of the House.
Lundquist said the proposal would not diminish the power of the initiative process.

"It simply aims to get objective information out," Lundquist, a Republican, said. "I believe the voters want to know if a measure they will vote on may be unconstitutional or if it has a fiscal impact that may affect their tax burden."
The report issued by the committee would not be binding on the initiative sponsors.
Parker said Lundquist's proposal could make it easier for Oregon to maintain and possibly raise its credit ratings.
Major credit rating agencies have expressed concerns about the current lack of "checks and balances" in the state's initiative process, Parker said.
